extraction.name: MATH Dataset
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems from high school math competitions (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, etc.) with step-by-step solutions in LaTeX and natural language. Designed to measure mathematical problem-solving ability in machine learning models.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.citeAs: Hendrycks, D., Burns, C., Kadavath, S., Arora, A., Basart, S., Tang, E., Song, D., & Steinhardt, J. (2021). Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset. arXiv:2103.03874.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Problems were collected from high school mathematics competitions including AMC 10, AMC 12, and AIME, spanning decades of competition problems. The problems were sourced from aops.com/community/c3158_usa_contests and curated to ensure they require advanced problem-solving techniques beyond standard K-12 tools.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mathematics competition problems from AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and other high school math competitions, sourced from aops.com/community/c3158_usa_contests.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Spans decades of competition problems (exact years not specified in the paper)
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Problems were normalized for formatting consistency, including consistent LaTeX encoding of mathematical expressions, standardized answer formatting (e.g., simplified fractions, specific fraction encoding), and normalization of equivalent mathematical expressions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problems were formatted using LaTeX and Asymptote for vector graphics. Answers were wrapped in \boxed{} command for automatic assessment. Formatting rules were established to ensure unique answers in a well-defined location, allowing for exact match evaluation. Problems were tagged by difficulty (1-5) and subject (Prealgebra, Algebra, Number Theory, Counting and Probability, Geometry, Intermediate Algebra, Precalculus).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem includes a full step-by-step solution written in LaTeX and natural language, providing detailed derivations and explanations. Solutions are used to teach models to generate answer derivations and explanations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: LaTeX for mathematical notation and Asymptote for vector graphics
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper notes that models trained on step-by-step solutions can generate coherent but often incorrect solutions, indicating challenges in converting raw annotations into reliable final labels.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 (each problem has one step-by-step solution and one final boxed answer)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LaTeX for mathematical notation, Asymptote for vector graphics, Mathematica for generating algorithmic problems and solutions, Khan Academy exercise framework for educational content
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released under MIT license with versioning information available at the GitHub repository (https://github.com/hendrycks/math). The paper states that the dataset and code for reproducing results are available, but does not specify explicit deprecation policies or update timeframes.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses that solving the MATH dataset would have profound practical and intellectual significance due to the broad reach and applicability of mathematics. It also notes potential ramifications if models achieve high accuracy on homework-like problems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges that the dataset may have biases inherent in competition mathematics problems, which are designed to assess the mathematical problem-solving ability of the best young mathematical talent in the United States. The problems may not represent the full diversity of mathematical thinking or problem-solving approaches.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) The dataset is challenging even for large language models, with accuracies ranging from 3.0% to 6.9% for state-of-the-art models. (2) Accuracy increases slowly with model size, suggesting that scaling alone may not solve the problem. (3) The problems are designed for human competition and may not generalize to real-world mathematical problem-solving scenarios. (4) The dataset does not cover all areas of mathematics equally, with some subjects like Prealgebra being easier than others like Precalculus.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use cases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Benchmarking for mathematical problem-solving in machine learning models. The dataset is intended to measure mathematical problem-solving ability and facilitate research in algorithmic advancements for mathematical reasoning. Usage guidelines emphasize that the dataset should not be used to train models that help students cheat on mathematics exams.
